pathways.climate_pressure: Pasture degradation and climatic stress in the dzud-resilience assessment.
pathways.documented_impact: Herders seek Otor pasture in other aimags as grazing access becomes constrained.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal access and limited systematic management of movement and shared pasture can mediate resource competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: The report describes disputes between incoming herders and local users, without event counts or armed-conflict evidence.
alternative_explanations: Herd size, grazing pressure and land-management arrangements also affect degradation and disputes.
Not all mobility or resource competition produces conflict.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative source-stated mechanism, not a measured climate-attributable conflict effect or a prediction for named receiving settlements.
resilience_factors: Transparent shared-pasture rules and monitoring are proposed governance responses, not evaluated conflict-reduction interventions.
pathways.compact_statement: Pasture stress and inter-aimag grazing mobility can interact with access and governance constraints to produce disputes; armed conflict is not established.

gaps: The grazing pathway is a bounded source-stated resource-governance mechanism, not a national causal estimate or armed-conflict classification.
GBV is retained as a protection issue without deriving a complete causal pathway from co-occurrence or ethnic stereotypes.

executive_assessment.text: Historical dzud mapping and small-herd survey results differentiate Sukhbaatar and Khovd within a four-aimag study; national impact figures are dated to 2023-2024.

The assessment describes pasture degradation and movement to Otor grazing areas interacting with access/governance constraints and disputes. This does not establish armed violence or make mobile herders a threat category.
Warning, local response, household coping and protection-service gaps coexist with reported outreach and training. Targets and outputs are not evaluated resilience or GBV-reduction effects.
